key_insight: Graph-compatible merging preserves at least 1/χ_f(G) of total verified local improvement, a tight guarantee for mergers selecting a subset of the same agent proposals.
engineering_relevance: Dependency-aware coordination can prevent parallel agents from undoing one another’s gains while exposing trade-offs among task structure, agent allocation, time, and cost.
method: Model shared work as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph.
Verify edits against the same current solution and use independent sets to identify edits whose gains add exactly.
Use fractional coloring for guaranteed merging, optionally evaluate interacting edits, and optimize agent assignment via a linear program.
evidence_signal: Code-repair tests demonstrated conflict resolution; road-network tests retained 922 units of verified graph-cut improvement across 90 paired runs, while route-search scheduling reduced wall time by a median 15% across 12 paired runs.
watch_item: The guarantees require a known dependency graph and exact objective evaluation; geometric convergence additionally depends on local-improvement and block error-bound assumptions.
paper_title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
